terms.grammar: present participle of circumstō used as a noun, usually plural
evidence: Quint. 4.2.22; Tac. Ann. 1.21; Suet. Caes. 84 (Lewis & Short s.v. circumstō)

terms.gloss: a mute character; a mere onlooker
terms.comment: Literally a non-speaking part; Traupman uses it of a bystander, someone who looks on and takes no part. Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections; the plain classical word is circumstantēs.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 285.
